facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case that the filings are enough for covenant and priority work is that they describe the first lien revolver's financial covenant, the guarantee and security terms of each facility and a summary of guarantor financials. That case fails where a creditor needs it most, because a filing's summary cannot show the definitions, baskets and carve-outs that decide headroom, or who is paid first in a default. Supplying the executed credit agreements and indentures, or current ratings and prices, would move covenant, priority and market-implied work from blocked to ready; a filing dated after 2026-11-05 that changed the debt stack would reopen the readiness of every module that relies on the third-quarter figures. facts.text: Cash generation, not interest, is the weak link. facts.label: Key findings

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest offset is management's statement that liquidity is adequate for the next twelve months, its expectation that working capital will be neutral over 2026, which implies a fourth-quarter inflow, and the savings it expects from the transformation plan. Against that, the same outlook names higher raw material costs, unabsorbed overhead and inflation in the fourth quarter, and nine-month operating cash flow was negative. A positive fourth-quarter operating cash flow with the 2027 notes repaid from cash, or segment operating income recovering toward its 2025 level, would improve the view; a further revolver draw to meet the 2027 maturity would worsen it. tables.title: Contrary evidence and what would change the view

rows.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view — paragraph 1
Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- High: The maturity ladder is printed only for 2026 to 2030 and only at year-end 2025, with no total contractual principal and no ladder at 30 September 2026. Contractual principal and its reconciliation to carrying value are therefore not stated, and the debt maturing after 2030 is not quantified; the two 2027 notes and the 2032 notes can be read from the instrument table, but a rolled-forward ladder was not built because it would require estimates. Closing it needs the executed agreements or a later annual report ladder. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 142; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22 - Medium: Goodyear states no EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or add-back schedule, so the leverage and cover figures use a derived, unadjusted EBITDA that includes impairments, restructuring and asset-sale gains. This restricts any conclusion on run-rate leverage and means no bridge from reported to adjusted EBITDA can be stated; an earnings release with company reconciliations would close it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 91; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2 - Medium: Cash interest paid is printed only for full years, so interest cover at 30 September 2026 and last-twelve-months cash interest are not calculable and no substitute is used. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 116 - Medium: The revised 2023 balance sheet is not in the supplied filings, so debt, cash, net debt and leverage are not stated at year-end 2023 and the 2023 column is shown for flows only; only the first-reported 2023 balance sheet exists in the 2024 annual report and mixing it with revised flows would be inconsistent. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 91–94; 10-K_2024-12-31_gt-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 104–105 - Medium: The debt stack omits the receivables securitization, the Mexican and Chinese facilities, other foreign and domestic debt, finance leases and notes payable and overdrafts because no filing states their legal rank, and the guarantor names sit in an exhibit that was not supplied. The stack therefore cannot establish creditor priority or structural subordination across the group. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 63–66 - Low: The quarterly report prints no discrete quarterly cash flow, no quarterly depreciation and amortization, no interest income and none of the annual-only investing and financing lines, so the quarterly columns are limited to the income statement figures shown in the financial metrics table and those cells are stated as not supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5 - Low: Source dashes (the nine-month 2026 goodwill impairment, assets held for sale at 2026-09-30, the insurance and sale-and-leaseback lines in 2025 and 2023, and Europe, Middle East and Africa segment operating income in nine months 2025) are kept as missing rather than zero; the totals tie without them. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 93–94 - Low: Restricted cash is not printed as a separate balance, the maintenance and growth capital expenditure split is not printed and no senior secured debt total can be built because other debt lines state no security; none is estimated. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22 - Low: The funded status of pension and retiree medical plans and the total of binding purchase commitments are printed only at year-end, so they are not updated to 30 September 2026 and the net deficit used here is a year-end figure. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 148; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 163; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30 - Low: Cash held in countries with transfer limits and the borrowing-base reduction of the first lien revolver restrict how much of the reported liquidity is freely available; the filings quantify them but the net effect on usable liquidity is not worked here. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56

facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Goodyear's credit profile has weakened sharply in 2026: net leverage on reported earnings reached 6.62x from 3.98x at year-end 2025 and cash flow is negative, so creditors rely on large undrawn lines rather than earnings to bridge the 2027 maturities. The strongest support is liquidity: USD 3,639 million of unused credit arrangements and USD 812 million of cash against USD 1,339 million due within a year. The weakest point is earnings: segment operating income fell to USD 305 million from USD 641 million in nine months, so net debt rose by USD 1,160 million, reversing 73.7% of the 2025 reduction. Whether the nine-month cash outflow is timing or structural will show in the fourth quarter. facts.label: Key findings

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Goodyear presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, recognised brands, a simpler perimeter and cash-preserving financial policy, but credit quality is constrained by negative cash flow, compressed margin and net leverage of 6.62x on reported earnings. Cash-flow durability appears weak due to three years of negative free cash flow and a 2.4% segment margin. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on revolver availability and the borrowing base, on the repayment of the 2027 notes and on market access at a higher coupon. The primary downside path is continued replacement weakness with adverse raw materials that prevents the fourth-quarter cash recovery, forcing more revolver use ahead of the 2028 maturities. Further analysis would require ratings, prices, the executed agreements, management projections and the proxy statement. spans.text: ## Request

Source readiness for Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co /Oh/ (the registrant, The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is whether the five supplied filings support the requested Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit work, and what stays blocked for other capabilities. No earlier run and no analysis from another module were supplied.
## Sources

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_gt-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the period ended 31 March 2026 | 2026-05-07 | 82805386cb6403db70ca793376a231e1709230c4cbf4fe1aa1831a711bb4548e | Unaudited first-quarter 2026 statements and notes; sequence and comparatives for the 2026 build; date is the signature date. |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the period ended 30 September 2026 | 2026-11-05 | 38d73bc27890bf356d002c4ca2526cd0230a2b94102ac683b975d82d31becc76 | Unaudited third-quarter and nine-month 2026 statements, financing note, liquidity, covenants and guarantor summary; latest evidence and the control for the current period; date is the signature date. |
No analysis from another module was supplied, so there is no upstream module to list.
## Findings
### Bottom line

The five filings support a credit snapshot of the consolidated Goodyear group through 30 September 2026 with limitations, so creditors can test liquidity and maturities from the filings but not covenant headroom or collateral priority against the governing documents. No executed debt agreements, credit ratings, current market prices or company-defined EBITDA were supplied.

The 2025 annual report revised 2024 earnings downward, so the revised figures, not those in the 2024 annual report, govern any comparison. The latest evidence is the third-quarter 2026 report, signed on 2026-11-05, thirteen days before the run date.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 166–167; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 75; calculation C1; calculation C2
### Key findings

The statements can be rolled to a last-twelve-months view at 30 September 2026 without a missing period, because the third-quarter report carries nine-month 2025 comparatives and the 2025 annual report carries the full year; only the fourth quarter of 2025 has to be derived by subtraction.

The issuer is one registrant, The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company, reporting consolidated figures for itself and its subsidiaries. The filings give no standalone accounts for the parent or a borrower group, only a summary of the parent and its guarantor subsidiaries, and the list of guarantors sits in an exhibit that was not supplied. The euro notes are issued by the European subsidiary with the parent as guarantor, so the issuer differs by instrument even though the consolidated figures are the only complete perimeter.

The third-quarter report prints each note series and the main credit facilities with amount, rate and maturity year, the borrowing-base shortfall on the first lien revolver, the covenant tests with a statement of compliance, receivables sold and supplier-finance balances, and the 2025 annual report adds a five-year maturity table. Liquidity and refinancing work therefore have what they need from the filings, though not from the agreements themselves.

The main claims outside reported debt each have their own disclosure in the filings: operating and finance leases, pension and retiree plans, receivables sold off balance sheet, supplier-finance programmes and the asbestos and product-liability reserves. Whether each sits inside or outside the debt figure is a question for Financial foundation, not for this readiness view.

No filing prints a group EBITDA, an adjusted EBITDA or the result of a covenant ratio; the covenants are described by name and threshold only, and their definitions sit in the credit agreements. Any EBITDA-based leverage or coverage figure will therefore be built from the statements and will not reconcile to the lenders' definition.

Business and governance work has the annual report's description of the operations, the three regional segments and the executive officers, and the quarterly segment tables, but no proxy statement, so director, shareholder and pay evidence is not established; the annual report defers those items to a proxy statement.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case that the filings are enough for covenant and priority work is that they describe the first lien revolver's financial covenant, the guarantee and security terms of each facility and a summary of guarantor financials. That case fails where a creditor needs it most, because a filing's summary cannot show the definitions, baskets and carve-outs that decide headroom, or who is paid first in a default. Supplying the executed credit agreements and indentures, or current ratings and prices, would move covenant, priority and market-implied work from blocked to ready; a filing dated after 2026-11-05 that changed the debt stack would reopen the readiness of every module that relies on the third-quarter figures.
### Limitations

- The figures were read from page-text extracts, not from the original formatted filings, and the extract of the 2024 annual report splits table cells across lines, so every figure carried into later work must be opened at its cited page.
- Only the two annual reports carry an audit opinion; the three quarterly reports are unaudited, so the nine-month 2026 position has a lower evidential standard than the year-end 2025 position.
- No document dated after the third-quarter report was supplied, so any financing, rating or trading event between 2026-11-05 and the 2026-11-18 cutoff is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 75; calculation C1

- MATERIAL: The executed credit agreements, indentures, security and guarantee documents were not supplied; the exhibit index lists them as incorporated by reference and the run settings declare no legal documents. Covenant headroom, guarantee and collateral priority therefore rest on the filings' summaries. Affected: Legal & covenants, Covenant capacity, Structural priority, Intercreditor control, Recovery & fulcrum and Security selection. Remediation: obtain the executed agreements and indentures from the exhibit index.

- MATERIAL: No current credit ratings, rating reports, trading prices, spreads or equity market data were supplied. The only equity market value is the aggregate for non-affiliates at 2025-06-30 on the annual report cover, and the filings give an aggregate fair value of long term debt at quoted prices without prices by series. Affected: Ratings & triggers, Market-implied risk, Security selection and Peer benchmark. Remediation: supply agency ratings, dated bond and equity prices and a peer set.

- MINOR: No filing prints a group EBITDA, an adjusted EBITDA or a covenant ratio result, and the definitions sit in agreements that were not supplied. Affected: Financial foundation, Liquidity and Covenant capacity, which must build EBITDA from the statements and label it as not the lenders' definition. Remediation: an earnings release with company EBITDA reconciliations, or the covenant compliance certificates.

- MINOR: The subsidiary list, the subsidiary guarantor list and the proxy statement were not supplied, so guarantor names, shareholders, directors and pay are not established. Affected: Business & governance and Structural priority. Remediation: the exhibit lists and the proxy statement.

- MINOR: Nothing dated after the third-quarter report was supplied, so events between 2026-11-05 and the 2026-11-18 cutoff are not established. Affected: every module that quotes the quarter-end position. Remediation: current reports and any earnings release after 2026-11-05.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 75; calculation C1

- MINOR: No management projections or user forecast assumptions were supplied; only full-year 2026 expectations for capital spending, interest, rationalization payments, taxes and pension contributions and a fourth-quarter outlook are printed. Affected: Forward credit model and Downside. Remediation: management or user forecast assumptions.

- Conflict, resolved by source rule: the 2025 annual report revised 2023 and 2024 amounts for errors in the currency remeasurement of the Turkish operations, so the 2024 annual report and the 2025 annual report print different 2024 values. The revised values control and the first-reported values are kept only as evidence of what was first reported, as set out below.

spans.text: ## Request

Financial foundation for Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co /Oh/ as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the consolidated statements for 2023 to 2025 and the first nine months of 2026, carrying-value debt, liquidity and leverage on derived reported EBITDA. Source readiness for the same run was supplied.
## Sources

Date is the signature date. |

No external sources were used.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Net leverage on reported EBITDA has jumped to 6.62x at 30 September 2026 from 3.98x at year-end 2025, because earnings fell while borrowing funded negative free cash flow, so creditors now carry more debt against a smaller earnings base. Net debt rose by USD 1,160 million in nine months to USD 6,557 million, while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA fell to USD 990 million from USD 1,357 million in 2025.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 92; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 91; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C07; calculation C08

Reported EBITDA is derived and distorted by one-off gains and impairments, so a segment-based proxy is shown beside it, and on that proxy net leverage still rises to 3.89x from 2.57x. The company states that liquidity is adequate for the next twelve months, but USD 1,339 million of debt falls due within a year, including the two 2027 notes.
Basis: calculation C18; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22
### Key findings

Leverage worsened from both sides of the ratio. Total debt rose by USD 1,171 million to USD 7,369 million, including the USD 1,050 million senior notes issued on 2026-06-04 and USD 676 million drawn on the two secured revolvers, while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA fell, so total debt over EBITDA reached 7.44x against 4.57x at year-end 2025.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C01; calculation C04; calculation C26; calculation C08

Cash generation, not interest, is the weak link. Free cash flow for the first nine months of 2026 was negative USD 1,245 million, made up of an operating outflow of USD 764 million and capital expenditure of USD 481 million, against negative USD 1,365 million a year earlier, and net borrowings of USD 1,209 million funded the gap. Receivables absorbed USD 711 million in the period; the company expects working capital to be neither a significant source nor use of cash over the full year, so the fourth quarter shows whether the outflow is timing or structural.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation C12; calculation C14

Reported EBITDA is a poor guide to run-rate earnings here because Goodyear states none and the derived figure keeps one-offs: 2025 includes USD 816 million of gains on asset sales and a USD 674 million goodwill impairment, and nine months 2025 includes USD 700 million of gains. On a proxy of segment operating income plus depreciation and amortization, which strips those items but also omits unallocated corporate costs, last-twelve-months earnings were USD 1,684 million against USD 2,102 million in 2025, a fall of USD 418 million, so both measures point to weaker earnings.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 91; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; calculation C06; calculation C17; calculation C19

Liquidity, meaning cash plus unused long term committed arrangements, fell to USD 4,138 million from USD 4,946 million at year-end 2025, mainly because the two revolvers, undrawn at year-end, carried USD 676 million at 30 September 2026. Of the USD 1,339 million due within a year, the two 2027 notes are USD 818 million due on 2027-03-15; the company intends to repay them with the proceeds of the 2026 notes, which it temporarily applied to repay revolver borrowings, so repayment depends on revolver and cash capacity rather than set-aside cash.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 134; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C16; calculation C15

Reported EBITDA covered cash interest 3.28x in 2025 and 3.30x in 2024. Cash interest paid for the nine months is not printed, so cover at 30 September 2026 is not established; interest expense for the last twelve months was USD 415 million against USD 445 million in 2025, and the 2032 notes carry the highest coupon of any note, so new unsecured debt is costing more.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 91; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; calculation C09; calculation C07

Funding outside the debt figure is material. Receivables of USD 844 million were sold off balance sheet and supplier-finance programmes confirmed USD 589 million, up from USD 551 million at year-end 2025 and included in trade payables, while operating lease liabilities of USD 1,000 million sit outside Total Debt. A withdrawal of factoring or supplier-finance capacity would draw on liquidity before it shows in reported debt.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 141; calculation C25

Other claims also sit outside the debt figure and outside the leverage ratios. Pension and retiree medical plans were net underfunded by USD 369 million at year-end 2025, with non-U.S. pensions USD 215 million and retiree medical USD 231 million in deficit and a U.S. pension surplus of USD 77 million; binding purchase commitments were about USD 5,500 million against USD 2,600 million a year earlier, including a 15-year take-or-pay chemical supply agreement; and reserves for asbestos and product liability were USD 435 million at 30 September 2026.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest offset is management's statement that liquidity is adequate for the next twelve months, its expectation that working capital will be neutral over 2026, which implies a fourth-quarter inflow, and the savings it expects from the transformation plan. Against that, the same outlook names higher raw material costs, unabsorbed overhead and inflation in the fourth quarter, and nine-month operating cash flow was negative. A positive fourth-quarter operating cash flow with the 2027 notes repaid from cash, or segment operating income recovering toward its 2025 level, would improve the view; a further revolver draw to meet the 2027 maturity would worsen it.
### Limitations

- Goodyear states no EBITDA, so the figure used is derived and unadjusted and keeps impairments, gains and restructuring inside it; no covenant EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA is available to set against it.

- Cash interest paid is printed for full years only, and the five-year maturity ladder stops at 2030 and is drawn at year-end 2025, so interest cover at 30 September 2026 and the reconciliation of contractual principal to carrying value are not established.

- The revised 2023 balance sheet is not in the supplied filings, so net debt and leverage are stated for 2024, 2025 and 30 September 2026 only; the 2024 and 2023 accounts were revised for a currency remeasurement error and the revised figures are used.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 166–167; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 92; Source readiness (CP-0)

## Gaps

- High: The maturity ladder is printed only for 2026 to 2030 and only at year-end 2025, with no total contractual principal and no ladder at 30 September 2026. Contractual principal and its reconciliation to carrying value are therefore not stated, and the debt maturing after 2030 is not quantified; the two 2027 notes and the 2032 notes can be read from the instrument table, but a rolled-forward ladder was not built because it would require estimates. Closing it needs the executed agreements or a later annual report ladder.

- Medium: Goodyear states no EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or add-back schedule, so the leverage and cover figures use a derived, unadjusted EBITDA that includes impairments, restructuring and asset-sale gains. This restricts any conclusion on run-rate leverage and means no bridge from reported to adjusted EBITDA can be stated; an earnings release with company reconciliations would close it.
- Medium: Cash interest paid is printed only for full years, so interest cover at 30 September 2026 and last-twelve-months cash interest are not calculable and no substitute is used.

- Medium: The revised 2023 balance sheet is not in the supplied filings, so debt, cash, net debt and leverage are not stated at year-end 2023 and the 2023 column is shown for flows only; only the first-reported 2023 balance sheet exists in the 2024 annual report and mixing it with revised flows would be inconsistent.

- Medium: The debt stack omits the receivables securitization, the Mexican and Chinese facilities, other foreign and domestic debt, finance leases and notes payable and overdrafts because no filing states their legal rank, and the guarantor names sit in an exhibit that was not supplied. The stack therefore cannot establish creditor priority or structural subordination across the group.

- Low: The quarterly report prints no discrete quarterly cash flow, no quarterly depreciation and amortization, no interest income and none of the annual-only investing and financing lines, so the quarterly columns are limited to the income statement figures shown in the financial metrics table and those cells are stated as not supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5

- Low: Source dashes (the nine-month 2026 goodwill impairment, assets held for sale at 2026-09-30, the insurance and sale-and-leaseback lines in 2025 and 2023, and Europe, Middle East and Africa segment operating income in nine months 2025) are kept as missing rather than zero; the totals tie without them.

- Low: Restricted cash is not printed as a separate balance, the maintenance and growth capital expenditure split is not printed and no senior secured debt total can be built because other debt lines state no security; none is estimated.

- Low: The funded status of pension and retiree medical plans and the total of binding purchase commitments are printed only at year-end, so they are not updated to 30 September 2026 and the net deficit used here is a year-end figure.

- Low: Cash held in countries with transfer limits and the borrowing-base reduction of the first lien revolver restrict how much of the reported liquidity is freely available; the filings quantify them but the net effect on usable liquidity is not worked here.

spans.text: ## Request

Business and transaction fact pack, with the sponsor and governance assessment, for Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co /Oh/ as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the registrant's business, ownership, corporate structure, transactions, new debt and shareholder and creditor behaviour, read from five filings through 30 September 2026. Source readiness for the same run was supplied.
## Sources

Date is the signature date. |

No external sources were used.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Goodyear is a widely held listed tire manufacturer with no sponsor or controlling shareholder identified, so creditors face operating and funding risk, not extraction risk, and the 2026 turn from debt repayment to net borrowing is the concern.

No common dividend has been paid since at least 2022, and the three 2025 divestitures raised about USD 2,220 million of gross proceeds that were applied to debt reduction. In the first nine months of 2026 the group borrowed USD 1,209 million net, including USD 1,050 million of senior notes due 2032, while segment operating income fell to USD 305 million from USD 641 million. Sponsor and governance risk is medium because owners, directors and legal capacity are not established, not because of adverse conduct.
### Key findings

No controlling shareholder or sponsor is identified, so sponsor extraction is not a documented risk, but ownership is unverified rather than disproved. The company is listed on Nasdaq with several thousand holders of record, and the proxy statement that would name large holders, directors and related-party dealings was not supplied.

Earnings have shifted from the Americas to Asia Pacific, which now carries the group. In the first nine months of 2026 the Americas produced 56.2% of net sales but 40.3% of segment operating income, down from 78.3% a year earlier, while Asia Pacific produced 11.5% of sales and 61.0% of segment operating income, up from 21.7%. Group segment operating margin was 2.4% against 4.8%.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; calculation C2; calculation C3

Demand risk sits in the replacement market, which is the larger and weaker part of the business. Replacement tires were 71.3% of 2025 units, and replacement volume fell 10.7% worldwide in the first nine months of 2026 while original-equipment volume rose 4.5%; management ascribes part of the fall to planned rationalization of lower-tier lines.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation C4

The 2025 portfolio sales reduced debt but left continuing obligations to each buyer. The sales of the off-the-road tire business, the Dunlop brand and the polymer chemicals business carry supply, licence, offtake or take-or-pay terms, binding purchase commitments were about $5.5bn at year-end 2025, and management expected the Dunlop and chemical sales to reduce 2026 segment operating income by about USD 185 million.

The June 2026 notes issue is meant to take out the 2027 maturities but did not set cash aside for them. The USD 1,050 million notes due 2032 are intended to repay the two 2027 notes, which total USD 818 million, yet the proceeds were first applied to revolver balances rather than held in cash, and the two revolvers carried USD 362 million at 30 June 2026 and USD 676 million at 30 September 2026. The annual coupon on the new notes is USD 93.19 million against USD 43.05 million on the two 2027 notes, an increase of USD 50.14 million, partly because the issue is larger than the notes it is meant to retire.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gt-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 134; calculation C7; calculation C8

Noteholders rely on a guarantor group whose summarized net sales equal 50.8% of group net sales and which ranks behind secured lenders and behind the foreign subsidiaries' own creditors. The senior notes are unsecured, guaranteed by wholly-owned United States and Canadian subsidiaries, and effectively subordinated to secured debt; the summarized guarantor group had net assets of USD 522 million at 30 September 2026 against USD 956 million at year-end 2025, and two older dollar notes totalling USD 268 million have no guarantee described. Net assets of USD 741 million, including USD 195 million of cash, sit in countries that require approval for transfers.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 63–66; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 55–56; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 135; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; calculation C9; calculation C10

Shareholder distributions are not a documented risk, and capital spending is being cut rather than financed. Capital expenditure fell to USD 826 million in 2025 from USD 1,188 million in 2024, and 2026 spending is now expected at about USD 675 million against about USD 825 million expected in February; management believes its capital spending relative to sales is below that of its principal competitors, which is an underinvestment risk. The credit facilities permit dividends and repurchases if no default exists and financial tests are met, and management states no current plans for either.

Restructuring is the main operating lever and carries a near-term cash cost. The Fayetteville plant closure approved on 2026-07-16 has total pre-tax charges of USD 535 million to USD 565 million, of which USD 190 million to USD 210 million is cash, and rationalization payments are expected to be about USD 210 million in 2026. A new master labour contract ratified on 2026-08-23 runs to 2029-04-28 for the three plants it covers; the filings do not reconcile its coverage with the earlier master agreement that was due to expire in July 2026.

Funding outside reported debt is large and has not grown in 2026, so it neither explains the cash outflow nor offers a new source, but it adds to liquidity needs if the programmes were withdrawn. Receivables sold off balance sheet and supplier finance confirmed together were USD 1,433 million at 30 September 2026 against USD 1,443 million at year-end 2025, and the confirmed supplier amounts sit in trade payables, not in debt.

Disclosure supports monitoring but not protection analysis. The 2025 annual report carries unqualified audit opinions on the statements and on internal control, yet 2023 and 2024 were revised for a currency remeasurement error that management judged not material, and covenant ratios are not printed, only a statement of compliance at 30 September 2026.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 88; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 61–62; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against a benign governance reading is that risk is untested, not low: the proxy statement is missing, the credit facilities allow distributions when tests are met, and nine months of borrowing show leverage rising with no distribution to explain it. The strongest case for a benign reading is that unused availability under all credit arrangements was USD 3,639 million at 30 September 2026, management states liquidity is adequate for twelve months, and no extraction, priming, exchange offer or covenant waiver is described in any of the five filings. A holder with board or consent rights in the proxy statement, any dividend or buyback, a transfer of assets outside the guarantor group, repayment of the 2027 notes from revolver draws, or a covenant waiver would move the view toward high; repayment of the 2027 notes from cash and a return of segment operating income in the Americas would move it toward low.
### Limitations

- The proxy statement and the exhibit that names the guarantor subsidiaries were not supplied, so the finding that no controlling holder exists means none identified, and the guarantor perimeter is described by class only; a holder with board rights or an unlisted guarantor would change both findings.

- The executed credit agreements and indentures were not supplied, so restricted-payment, debt and lien capacity is stated only as the filings summarize it; a broad basket or an unrestricted-subsidiary right would move the governance rating toward high even though no distribution has been made.

- Comparisons of 2026 with 2025 mix retained and divested operations because no pro forma accounts were supplied, so the fall in group sales and the shift of earnings toward Asia Pacific overstate or understate the underlying trend by an amount not quantified here.

- No customer, channel or distributor share of sales is stated, so the conclusion that revenue is diversified by region and product does not extend to customers; a dominant vehicle maker or distributor would raise business risk.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6–8

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The only new debt issue in 2026 is USD 1,050 million of senior notes due 2032-07-15, issued on 2026-06-04 at par. They are unsecured senior obligations of the parent, guaranteed by the United States and Canadian subsidiaries that also guarantee the first lien revolver, callable from 2029-07-15 at a premium that falls to par from 2031-07-15, and the indenture limits liens, sale and leaseback transactions and mergers. Management intends to use the proceeds to repay, redeem or repurchase the two notes due 2027-03-15, USD 700 million and USD 118 million as printed, at or before maturity; meanwhile the proceeds were applied to revolver balances, which stood at USD 362 million at 30 June 2026 and USD 676 million at 30 September 2026. The new coupon is higher than the coupons on the notes it is meant to retire, by USD 50.14 million a year on the stated principal amounts.

In 2025 the group issued USD 500 million of senior notes due 2030 on 2025-06-03, redeemed USD 500 million of notes due 2025 on 2025-02-19 and redeemed USD 900 million of notes due 2026 in two steps on 2025-06-30 and 2025-07-03, all at par, and extended the first lien revolver to 2030-05-19 and the European receivables securitization to 2032-10-18. Net debt repayments were USD 1,759 million, funded from the 2025 sale proceeds. The securitization's back-up liquidity commitments still expire in October 2027, so its funding of USD 228 million at 30 September 2026 depends on renewal of those commitments.

The three 2025 divestitures were the off-the-road tire business sold to Yokohama on 2025-02-03 for USD 905 million, the Dunlop brand rights sold to Sumitomo Rubber Industries on 2025-05-07 for a USD 526 million purchase price and USD 735 million of gross proceeds at closing, and the polymer chemicals business sold on 2025-10-31 for USD 650 million with about USD 580 million of gross cash at closing. Together they raised about USD 2,220 million of gross proceeds. Each carries continuing obligations: a supply agreement of up to five years and a ten-year trademark licence to Yokohama, a transition licence, up to five years of offtake and a commercial-tire licence back from Sumitomo, and a 15-year take-or-pay supply agreement with the chemical buyer.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 42–44; 10-K_2024-12-31_gt-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C5

No acquisition, merger or sponsor transaction is described in 2026, no pro forma leverage is stated for any transaction, and no event after the third-quarter report of 2026-11-05 is covered. The date and price of the Cooper Tire acquisition are not stated in the supplied filings; the traces are the 7.625% notes that Goodyear assumed on 2022-11-25 and USD 435 million of indefinite-lived intangible assets from that acquisition at the 2024 impairment test.

- Material: The executed credit agreements and indentures were not supplied, so restricted-payment, investment, debt, lien, asset-transfer and unrestricted-subsidiary capacity are known only as the filings summarize them, and legal capacity cannot be separated from willingness. ## Findings
### Bottom line

Goodyear's credit profile has weakened sharply in 2026: net leverage on reported earnings reached 6.62x from 3.98x at year-end 2025 and cash flow is negative, so creditors rely on large undrawn lines rather than earnings to bridge the 2027 maturities.

The strongest support is liquidity: USD 3,639 million of unused credit arrangements and USD 812 million of cash against USD 1,339 million due within a year. The weakest point is earnings: segment operating income fell to USD 305 million from USD 641 million in nine months, so net debt rose by USD 1,160 million, reversing 73.7% of the 2025 reduction. Whether the nine-month cash outflow is timing or structural will show in the fourth quarter.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C5; calculation C8; calculation C11
### Key findings

Leverage has moved from moderate to stretched on reported earnings, and the earnings measure itself is uncertain. Net debt was USD 6,557 million at 30 September 2026 against USD 5,397 million at year-end 2025, while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, which Goodyear does not state and which includes asset-sale gains and impairments, fell to USD 990 million from USD 1,357 million. Net debt over that measure is 6.62x against 3.98x; over segment operating income plus depreciation, which strips the one-offs but omits corporate costs, it is 3.89x against 2.57x, and which is closer to lender definitions is not established.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 91–94; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4

Earnings fell because volume and fixed-cost absorption moved against Goodyear faster than savings could offset. Segment operating income was USD 305 million against USD 641 million, a margin of 2.4% against 4.8%; conversion costs rose by USD 458 million as production fell and replacement volume dropped 10.7%, while the transformation plan delivered USD 292 million and price and mix USD 152 million. The Americas earned 40.3% of segment income against 78.3% a year earlier, and Asia Pacific 61.0% against 21.7%.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 44–45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; calculation C5; calculation C6

Cash flow, not interest, is the binding constraint, and part of the nine-month outflow is timing. Free cash flow was USD -1,245 million in nine months after USD 871 million of working capital use, yet in 2025 the same nine months were USD -1,365 million and the fourth quarter then produced USD 1,335 million; management expects working capital to be neutral over 2026, so the fourth quarter decides whether the outflow reverses. Stated 2026 cash needs for capital spending, interest, restructuring, taxes and pensions total USD 1,510 million, or 89.7% of last-twelve-months segment operating income plus depreciation, before unallocated corporate costs.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; calculation C7; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C20

Liquidity is adequate for the next twelve months but is secured and partly conditional. Unused availability of USD 3,639 million includes USD 2,422 million under the first lien revolver, which is USD 270 million below its stated size because of a borrowing base, and USD 195 million of cash sits in countries that restrict transfers; the springing interest-cover test does not apply because availability plus available cash is USD 2,476 million against a USD 275 million trigger. USD 1,339 million falls due within a year, including the two 2027 notes totalling USD 818 million due 2027-03-15.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 54–56; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; calculation C11; calculation C12

Refinancing depends on revolver capacity and market access rather than on cash set aside. The June 2026 issue of USD 1,050 million of notes due 2032 was applied first to revolver balances, which rose from USD 362 million at 30 June 2026 to USD 676 million at 30 September 2026, and its annual coupon is USD 50.14 million higher than that of the notes it is meant to retire. After 2027, USD 1,224 million falls due in 2028, including the European revolver, and the securitization's back-up commitments expire in October 2027.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-06-30_gt-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13; calculation C14

Noteholders sit behind secured lenders and foreign creditors, and claims outside debt add to the fixed burden. The notes are unsecured and structurally subordinated; the guarantor group's net assets fell to USD 522 million from USD 956 million in nine months. Receivables sold and supplier finance total USD 1,433 million, operating leases USD 1,000 million, the pension and retiree medical deficit USD 369 million and binding purchase commitments about $5.5bn, none of which is in reported debt.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 63–66; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 148; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 163; calculation C15; calculation C16

Business quality is average rather than weak, and financial policy is not the source of the problem. Scale, recognised brands, a simpler perimeter after three sales and no distributions support the view, but capital spending of USD 481 million in nine months is 0.66 times depreciation, which cannot continue without eroding the footprint, and governance evidence on owners and legal capacity remains incomplete.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; calculation C17
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against a weakening view is timing: the fourth quarter of 2025 produced USD 1,335 million of free cash flow after nine months of USD -1,365 million, management expects neutral working capital for 2026, further transformation savings of about USD 110 million are expected in the fourth quarter, tariff refunds were received in 2026, and Asia Pacific segment income rose to USD 186 million from USD 139 million. Against that, management also expects raw materials to be USD 170 million worse and unabsorbed overhead USD 45 million higher in the fourth quarter, and the 2025 comparison included deferred cash from the three sales that will not recur. A fourth-quarter inflow that brings year-end net debt back toward the USD 5,397 million of year-end 2025, repayment of the 2027 notes from cash and stabilising replacement volume would move the view toward average; a further revolver draw to meet the 2027 maturity, a wider borrowing-base shortfall or a larger fourth-quarter outflow would move it toward weak.
### Limitations

- No rating, trading price or peer financials were supplied, so statements about Goodyear against typical leveraged issuers and about market access beyond the two recent note issues are not established; a peer set would change the business-profile assessment.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- The outlook and the downside scenario rest on management's fourth-quarter statements and on a nine-month run-rate; no projection or user assumption was supplied, so the timing of any cash recovery is not forecast and the scenario shows direction and scale, not probability.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The seasonal pattern of cash flow, a large fourth-quarter inflow after weak nine months, is observed for 2025 alone because nine-month cash flow for earlier years was not supplied, and the 2025 inflow included deferred cash from the divestitures; the timing argument is therefore one observation, not a trend.

- Contingent claims, namely the European Commission investigation, the environmental notice for the former chemical plant and unreserved asbestos or product liability, are described but only reserves are sized, so the downside excludes any settlement above them.
### Strengths and weaknesses
Strengths are ranked by their weight in the credit view.

Liquidity is the main support. Unused credit arrangements of USD 3,639 million and cash of USD 812 million cover the USD 1,339 million due within a year 3.32 times, so a missed fourth quarter does not force a financing in the next twelve months; the limits are that USD 270 million of first lien availability is lost to the borrowing base and USD 195 million of cash sits behind transfer limits.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 54–56; calculation C11; calculation C12

The 2025 portfolio sales cut debt and simplified the group. Gross proceeds of USD 2,220 million funded net debt repayments of USD 1,759 million, removed the 2025 and 2026 note maturities and let the first lien revolver be extended to 2030, which lowers refinancing pressure until 2027.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 42–44; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 60; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C19

Financial policy preserves cash. No dividend or buyback has been paid since at least 2022, capital expenditure fell 30.5% in 2025 and is guided to about USD 675 million for 2026, which gives a lever if cash flow worsens, although it risks competitiveness.

Scale and cost actions remain. Net sales were USD 17,588 million over the last twelve months, three regional businesses and recognised brands remain, and the transformation plan delivered about $1.5bn of run-rate cost benefit with USD 292 million more in nine months of 2026.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40

Market access was shown twice. Goodyear placed USD 500 million of unsecured notes in June 2025 and USD 1,050 million in June 2026 at par, although the later issue carried a much higher coupon than the notes it replaces.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 136; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; calculation C14
Weaknesses are ranked by their weight in the credit view.

Cash generation is negative and has been for three years. Free cash flow was USD -18 million in 2023, USD -490 million in 2024 and USD -30 million in 2025, and USD -1,245 million in nine months of 2026, so debt service has relied on asset sales and borrowing.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; calculation C7

Earnings are compressed and thin. Segment operating margin was 2.4% in nine months of 2026, and fixed-cost absorption, raw materials and tariffs act together, so a small further fall in volume moves margin disproportionately.
Leverage is high and rising on reported earnings: 6.62x on derived EBITDA and 3.89x on the segment proxy, with net debt up USD 1,160 million in nine months.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C4

The 2027 and 2028 maturities are not pre-funded. USD 818 million falls due on 2027-03-15 and USD 1,224 million in 2028, and the repayment source is revolver capacity at a time when the borrowing base is already USD 270 million short.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–24; calculation C13

Structural position and fixed claims weigh on noteholders. The notes are unsecured and behind secured lenders and foreign creditors, earnings are increasingly concentrated in Asia Pacific, and USD 1,433 million of off-balance-sheet funding, USD 1,000 million of operating leases and a USD 369 million pension deficit rank alongside them.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 63–66; calculation C6; calculation C15; calculation C16

### Business and revenue durability

Goodyear makes and sells tires in three regions; tire units were 84% of 2025 net sales and replacement tires were 71.3% of 2025 units, so revenue follows replacement demand, which is discretionary, price-competitive and weak in 2026. Replacement volume fell 10.7% worldwide in nine months, partly by design as lower-tier lines are rationalised, while original-equipment volume rose 4.5%; price and mix added USD 267 million to net sales, which shows pricing support but not enough to hold margin. Net sales fell 5.2% in nine months, helped by price and mix and hurt by the Dunlop and chemical sales and lower volume.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 44–45; calculation C5; calculation C6

No customer or channel concentration is disclosed and the business is not seasonal to a significant degree, so revenue visibility rests on the volume trend rather than on contracts. The credit linkage is moderate cash-flow visibility with no contracted base, so debt service depends on volume stabilising and on cost actions rather than on recurring revenue.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6–8; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Ownership and group structure

Goodyear is a widely held listed company with no sponsor or controlling holder identified, so the financial-policy risk that sponsor ownership usually brings is not documented, while owners, directors and legal capacity are not established and the governance level is medium. The parent issues most dollar notes, a European subsidiary issues the euro notes, and wholly-owned United States and Canadian subsidiaries guarantee the first lien revolver and most notes.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63

The guarantor group's summarized net sales equal 50.8% of group net sales and its net assets fell from USD 956 million to USD 522 million in nine months, so noteholders depend on a perimeter that is shrinking in net assets and ranks behind secured lenders and the foreign subsidiaries' own creditors. Two older dollar notes totalling USD 268 million have no guarantee described.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 63–66; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 134–135; calculation C16
### Cost structure, margin resilience and cash conversion

Costs are largely fixed in the short run: lower production raised conversion costs by USD 458 million in nine months while the transformation plan saved USD 292 million. Raw materials were USD 150 million favourable in nine months but management expects USD 170 million adverse in the fourth quarter, and the annual tariff cost was forecast at about USD 300 million for 2026, so margin can be defended only if volume stabilises; about 57.1% of associates are under collective bargaining and closures carry cash cost.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 46; calculation C5; calculation C21

Capital spending was USD 481 million in nine months against depreciation of USD 731 million, 0.66 times, and USD 826 million in 2025 against USD 1,045 million, 0.79 times, so capex flexibility has been used and cannot be repeated without eroding the footprint. Stated 2026 needs for capital spending, interest, restructuring payments, taxes and pension contributions total USD 1,510 million, which is 89.7% of last-twelve-months segment operating income plus depreciation before unallocated corporate costs, so EBITDA converts poorly into free cash flow available for debt reduction.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C17
### Competitive forces and external factors

Rivalry is high: Bridgestone and Michelin are the two major competitors, others make tires in low-cost countries and lower-tier imports have raised competition in the United States, which limits price recovery and makes volume and absorption the swing factors. New entrants matter mainly as lower-tier imports from Asia. Substitutes are not a near-term credit factor, although electric and autonomous vehicles may require new products. Buyer power is not established because no customer share is stated, and supplier power rose after the chemical sale because synthetic rubber is now bought under a 15-year take-or-pay contract.

Political and economic factors are material: annualised tariff cost of about USD 300 million for 2026 is forecast, refunds of an estimated USD 60 million of tariffs were recognised, inflation keeps conversion and transport costs high and about 19% of debt bears variable rates averaging 6.10%. Social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials.

In credit terms the strengths are liquidity, the simpler perimeter after three sales and cash-preserving policy; the weaknesses are negative cash flow, thin margin and leverage; the opportunities are original-equipment share gains, Asia Pacific income growth and further savings; the threats are replacement weakness, raw-material and tariff costs and fixed purchase commitments.
### Financial profile

Scale and market position are average: net sales were USD 17,588 million over the last twelve months in three regions, but no market share is stated and two major competitors are named. Competitive advantage is average: the brands are recognised, yet management believes its footprint is less cost-competitive. Business diversification is average: three regions and a mix of replacement and original-equipment tires, against 85.0% of sales from tire units and 46.4% from the United States.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C2; calculation C6

Cost and capex flexibility are average: capex was cut 30.5% in 2025 and fixed costs are being cut through closures, but absorption is the main pressure. Margin stability is weak: segment operating margin fell from 6.9% in 2024 to 5.8% in 2025 and to 2.4% in nine months of 2026. Free cash flow stability is weak: it was negative in each of 2023, 2024 and 2025 and in nine months of 2026.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; calculation C7; calculation C17

Ability to refinance is average: Goodyear placed notes in 2025 and 2026 at par, but the 2026 coupon is much higher and no rating or price was supplied. Liquidity position is average, close to adequate: cash and unused availability cover the amounts due within a year 3.32 times but is secured and collateral-dependent. Financial policy and governance are average: no distributions and capex cuts, offset by rising net borrowing and incomplete evidence on owners and legal capacity.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11; calculation C14
### Outlook

Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the tailwinds are about USD 110 million of further transformation savings in the fourth quarter and about USD 300 million expected for 2026, lower capital spending, one-off tariff refunds, original-equipment share gains and Asia Pacific income growth; the headwinds are weak replacement volume, USD 170 million of adverse raw materials and USD 110 million of other inflation in the fourth quarter, tariffs, the loss of about USD 185 million of 2026 segment income from the Dunlop and chemical sales, restructuring cash of about USD 210 million in 2026 and the 2027 and 2028 maturities. A master labour contract ratified on 2026-08-23 runs to 2029-04-28 for the plants it covers and a closing agreement with the tax authority on 2026-07-29 ended a proposed USD 1.5 billion income disallowance without a material cash effect. The stated fourth-quarter items net to USD 215 million of pressure against the fourth quarter of 2025, before price and mix and volume effects that management does not quantify.

Over three to five years the main question is whether the lower cost base and smaller footprint restore margin before the 2029 and 2030 maturities of USD 850 million and USD 557 million; the filings state no medium-term target or forecast, so this horizon is not assessable beyond the maturity ladder.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; calculation C13
### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is that replacement volume keeps falling and raw materials turn against Goodyear as management expects in the fourth quarter. The first operational break is a fourth-quarter segment operating income below the USD 416 million of the fourth quarter of 2025 because stated cost headwinds exceed planned savings by USD 215 million, so inventory of USD 3,748 million and receivables of USD 3,081 million are not converted into the cash that management assumes for a neutral working-capital year.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation C18

Financial transmission follows: operating cash flow stays negative, net borrowing continues, the revolvers move above USD 676 million, and the first lien borrowing base, which depends on receivables and inventory, would not give back its USD 270 million shortfall. If nine-month cash burn persisted with no seasonal recovery, an upper-bound stress rather than a forecast, free cash flow of USD -1,660 million over twelve months plus USD 1,339 million due would use USD 2,999 million of the USD 4,451 million of cash and unused lines, and a second such year with USD 1,224 million due in 2028 would exceed what is left by USD 1,432 million. The observable triggers are quarterly operating cash flow, the revolver balance, the borrowing-base shortfall, how the 2027 notes are repaid and the coupon on any new issue.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C11; calculation C13; calculation C22

Management levers are further capital-spending cuts, more plant closures, a larger working-capital release and asset sales, although the three large sales are done and no further sale candidates are named. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through the 2027 maturity even if the nine-month outflow repeated, but it is not sufficient to fund a second year of such outflow and the 2028 maturities without recovery or refinancing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 42–44; calculation C22
### Overall credit view

Overall, Goodyear presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, recognised brands, a simpler perimeter and cash-preserving financial policy, but credit quality is constrained by negative cash flow, compressed margin and net leverage of 6.62x on reported earnings. Cash-flow durability appears weak due to three years of negative free cash flow and a 2.4% segment margin. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on revolver availability and the borrowing base, on the repayment of the 2027 notes and on market access at a higher coupon. The primary downside path is continued replacement weakness with adverse raw materials that prevents the fourth-quarter cash recovery, forcing more revolver use ahead of the 2028 maturities. Further analysis would require ratings, prices, the executed agreements, management projections and the proxy statement.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C5; calculation C7; calculation C22
Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: the fourth-quarter cash recovery fails and the 2027 maturity is met from revolver capacity.

- Material: No credit rating, bond price, spread or peer financials were supplied, so the comparison of Goodyear with typical leveraged issuers, the cost of market access beyond the two recent notes and any rating-linked terms are not established; the profile is stated from the filings alone. Closing it needs agency ratings, dated prices and a peer set.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22

- Material: The executed credit agreements, indentures and covenant definitions were not supplied, so covenant headroom, restricted-payment capacity and legal priority are not assessed and the leverage figures are not lender measures. Closing it needs the agreements and covenant compliance certificates.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 61–62; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Minor: Management projections and user forecast assumptions were not supplied, so the outlook and downside rest on management's fourth-quarter statements and a nine-month run-rate, and no forecast of free cash flow, margin or leverage is made.

- Minor: Nine-month cash flow for years before 2025 was not supplied, so the size of the normal fourth-quarter working-capital release is observed once, for 2025, and was helped by deferred cash from the divestitures.
- Minor: No customer, channel or distributor share of sales is stated, so buyer power and revenue concentration are not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6–8
